points: This jumps back to the fourth year of Yehoyakim. Hashem tells Yirmiyahu to write his message in a book. Chazal say it was Megillas Eichah.
Baruch ben Neriah writes it and reads it in the Bais Hashem on a fast day. The ministers are moved, and they tell Yirmiyahu and Baruch to hide.
The king, in his winter palace, listens calmly until the fourth pasuk, which is about the leaders. Then he cuts up the scroll and burns it.
Contrast his father Yoshiyahu, who heard the Torah's warnings and tore his own clothes. Yehoyakim tore the message instead, and his son rules only three months.
Yirmiyahu writes Eichah again and adds more. When enemies try to crush Torah, it comes back stronger, like Kabbalah flourishing in Tzfas after the expulsion from Spain.
